clue.text: Off to make top hats?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a playful reading: hats at the top end of style

parts.note: meat or game that has gone off is said to be high
to fashion something is to make or shape it

explanation.surface: A grumble that something is off, and a question about how top hats get made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' looks like a departure but means gone bad, as with game hung too long. The definition is whimsical: the most stylish headgear belongs to the world of couture.
explanation.definitionFit: Couture at its most exclusive is the top end of style, so its hats are literally 'top' hats in a punning sense.

clue.text: In a word, what Debora ultimately seems to lack?

definitions.text: In a word, what Debora ultimately seems to lack?

parts.words: In a word, what Debora ultimately seems to lack?
parts.note: the name Deborah is usually spelt with a final H, missing here; in the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter H is spelt out as a word

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a misspelt name and what it is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' points at the end of the name: the usual spelling ends in H, and 'In a word' asks for that letter as spoken in the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators say this word for the eighth letter, which is exactly what the shortened spelling of the name lacks.

clue.text: Cricket side happy to drop last limited overs captain

indicators.note: the synonym for happy loses its final letter, as the clue says it must drop its last

parts.note: happy means glad
Eoin Morgan captained England's one-day (limited overs) cricket side

explanation.surface: A cheerful cricket team about to lose its one-day skipper.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAD loses its last letter to give GLA, followed by MORGAN. Glamorgan is the Welsh county side in English first-class cricket; 'limited overs' means one-day matches.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh county club plays in English domestic cricket, so it is a cricket team.

clue.text: Beastly bit of recording in first half of Frowning Atahuallpa's intro, sadly

indicators.note: in places the recording within the rearranged letters
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
the opening half of the word Frowning is taken
an intro is the start, so only the opening letter of the Inca's name is used

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A frowning Inca emperor introduced sadly, with a bit of recording slipped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges FROWA into FORAW. Atahuallpa was the last Inca emperor; 'Beastly' is a pun meaning belonging to a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's front foot is a part of a beast, hence a beastly bit in the literal sense.

clue.text: Lily as climbing flower? That's Electric Warrior

indicators.note: in a down clue a climbing flower grows upward, so the lily and the word as are read from the bottom up

parts.note: the arum is a type of lily
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A lily posing as a climbing plant, with a nod to the T. Rex album Electric Warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing flower' reads the pieces upwards as SAMURA. 'Electric Warrior' looks like the album title but splits: one word gives current, the other is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Japan's old military caste was a professional fighting man.

clue.text: Singer getting home late

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
late can mean former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A vocalist arriving home late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is not a vocalist: in slang, to sing is to tell the police what you know.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a grass who tells all to the police is said to sing.

clue.text: Figures writer must be out of range

indicators.note: the writer has to leave the mountain range, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the Pennines are a range of hills in northern England
a pen is a writer

explanation.surface: An author who must leave a cooking range, or be out of range of a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines, the hill chain running down northern England, lose PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerals such as 9 are figures, and the plural is the word for several of that digit.

clue.text: A fellow setter had a point: 25 must be upset about current view of Britain from Barnier's people

definitions.text: view of Britain from Barnier's people

parts.note: a can mean per, as in ten pounds a head
the setter refers to himself as I, and I had shortens to I'd
E is a point of the compass

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged name surrounds the current
upset means knocked over, so the letters of the surname are rearranged

parts.note: 25 across is the second part of the rocker's name
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A setter boasting he had a point about the theme rocker, then turning to French views of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLAN rearranged gives ALBON, and 'about' puts I inside it. Michel Barnier was the EU's Brexit negotiator, so his people are the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase 'perfidious Albion' casts Britain as treacherous, a long-standing French jibe.

clue.text: Younger female sailor fed to bull by king? That was monstrous!

indicators.note: fed to means placed inside, so the younger female sailor goes into the bull

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac
yr is an abbreviation for younger
Ann is a typical female name
OS is an ordinary seaman
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A sacrificial tale of a young woman sailor fed to a bull by a king, which was monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed to' puts the three short pieces inside the zodiac bull. The exclamation hints at a monster, and at the theme band named after one.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest meat-eating dinosaur was a creature of monstrous size, extinct, hence 'was'.

clue.text: Former leader of 8 32 has a walk-on part

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the leader of each of the two cross-referenced entries is its opening letter

parts.note: 8 down is the first word of the dinosaur's name
32 across is the Latin word for king ending the name

explanation.surface: The former frontman of the band T. Rex reduced to a bit part.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one name, 8 32 is the band, but 'leader of' picks the opening letter of each light separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A film walk-on is a non-speaking background role, played by someone hired just for the crowd.

clue.text: Memory? It'll be right in the morning

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A worry about memory loss, with reassurance that things will be fine by morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Random-access memory is a computer's working store, so it is memory in the computing sense.

clue.text: Georgia's evil-smelling jelly, after horseplay

definitions.note: the US state stands for American usage, where the adjective means smelly

indicators.note: after tells us the jelly comes second, following the horseplay

parts.note: horseplay is rough fun
KY is a brand of lubricating jelly

explanation.surface: A smelly jelly from Georgia served up after some boisterous games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the jelly second. Georgia, a US state, flags an Americanism; KY is a well-known brand of lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang the adjective first meant musty or stinking before it came to describe soul music.

clue.text: Fear LSD trip finally unhinged rock band?

indicators.note: unhinged means deranged, so the letters are disordered
finally picks the last letter of trip

explanation.surface: A rock band's acid trip ending with them all unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: FEARLSD plus P is rearranged. The definition plays on the theme: the answer is a mineral that forms bands in rock, not a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: This common silicate mineral runs in layers through granite and other rocks, so it is a band within rock.

clue.text: See 12
One religiously following, from afar, a star

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A devotee following a star seen from afar, like the Magi.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Jamaican faith that reveres Haile Selassie is devoted to a religion.

clue.text: Finally went and acted after taking tablet

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the tablet goes inside

parts.note: did means acted
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Someone who acted after swallowing a pill and was finally gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally went' reads like a last-letter instruction, but it is the definition: went for good.
explanation.definitionFit: To go finally is a euphemism for passing away.

clue.text: Finish letter to daughter

parts.note: en is the spelt-out name of the letter N

explanation.surface: Completing a letter to one's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of something is its finish, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: See 27
A layer of the netherworld

indicators.note: of signals the letters are part of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A level of the underworld, like one of Dante's circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird kept for eggs is one that lays them, hence a layer.

clue.text: Setter's comment: "It won't finish in court"

indicators.note: the bark is cut short without its final letter

parts.note: a setter is a dog, whose comment is a bark

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's remark that a legal case won't conclude in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay suit to someone with a view to romance is to court them.

clue.text: Arms whirling on dancer

indicators.note: whirling spins things round, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A dancer whirling with arms outstretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' looks like limbs in the dance but means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Military weapons and artillery collectively are the munitions sense of arms.

clue.text: Like former council member in tree, frantically busy

parts.note: the alder is a tree
manic means frantically busy

explanation.surface: A former councillor up a tree, run off their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldermen were senior members of English borough councils before their abolition; the adjective describes such officials.

clue.text: Gold earring turns up by the end of four dawns

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
in a down clue turns up means read from the bottom up

parts.note: an ear and a ring, the ring being the letter O

explanation.surface: A gold earring catching the light at the fourth dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: AU and R, then EAR plus O read upwards as ORAE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for daybreak, personified as its goddess, has this plural for several dawns.

clue.text: Like some books about Kiss? For sure

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the kiss sits inside

parts.note: indeed means for sure
X is a kiss

explanation.surface: A question about books on the rock band Kiss, answered with certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiss' suggests the rock band, but it is just the letter X used for a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Reference books often have an alphabetical list of topics at the back, so they are furnished with one.

clue.text: Dances if Hot Love plays, wanting sexual partner

parts.note: H is an abbreviation for hot, as on taps
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the partner is removed

parts.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner

explanation.surface: People dancing when the T. Rex song Hot Love plays, minus a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot Love was a T. Rex number one; here its two words split into single letters. 'wanting' leaves PS.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal dances, like a sock hop, are called this, from the bouncy steps.

clue.text: See 30
By the sound of it, would I see reason?

parts.note: would sounds like wood, and a log is a piece of wood

indicators.note: the words are to be heard, not read: would sounds like wood and see like the letter

parts.note: see is said the same as the letter C

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they would see sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Heard aloud, 'would I see' is 'wood I C'; a log is wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational thought and sound argument are what reason means as a noun.

clue.text: Hit by thought, with answer falling out

definitions.text: Hit by thought, with answer falling out

indicators.note: falling out suggests the pieces tumble loose and are rearranged

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A song that came from an idea, with the answer simply dropping out.
explanation.walkthrough: HIT, IDEA, W and ANSWER are rearranged together. The whole clue also describes a T. Rex hit that came from a flash of inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: This T. Rex single of 1970 was a chart success, so the clue's 'Hit' names it.

clue.text: Teacher in wig, retired by university

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig

explanation.surface: A teacher in a wig, pensioned off by the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu spiritual guide is a teacher, and by extension any revered mentor.

clue.text: Detachments from hand and foot, say

definitions.meaning: military detachments are groups of soldiers
a hand and a foot are both measures of length

explanation.surface: Something cut off from a hand and a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand, used for horses' heights, is four inches; a foot is twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodies of troops are detachments, and standard measures like the hand are measurements; both are this word.

clue.text: Rocker found in crashed car — no blame, no drug involved

indicators.note: crashed suggests wreckage, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A rock star killed in a car crash, with no one to blame and no drugs involved.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR NO BLAME holds the answer's letters plus E, which 'no drug involved' removes. The singer died in a car crash in 1977.
explanation.definitionFit: This glam rock star fronted T. Rex, so he was a rock musician.

clue.text: See 2
See 8
Farewell notice that is for all to see

parts.note: an ad is a notice
i.e. means that is
U is the British film rating for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A goodbye notice posted where everyone can read it.
explanation.walkthrough: A U certificate in Britain means a film is suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: The French leave-taking word is used in English as a goodbye.

clue.text: Suddenly becomes clear about always beginning to distrust know-it-alls

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the inner pieces sit inside

parts.note: something that clicks suddenly makes sense
ever means always

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone realising, suddenly, that they always distrust smart alecs.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug show-offs who think they have all the answers are smart alecs, a synonym.
